key_insight: NeuroGRIP improves EEG seizure diagnosis by using retrieved clinical knowledge to refine noisy graph connections and make predictions more interpretable.
clinical_relevance: By grounding EEG graph decisions in guideline-derived biomedical knowledge, the approach may support more clinically plausible and explainable seizure detection.
method: Builds a domain-specific knowledge graph from authoritative clinical guidelines
Uses STGNN EEG node embeddings to form semantic queries against the knowledge base
Scores and prunes predicted edges using retrieved similarity, relation type, and source reliability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive evaluation on TUSZ and CHB-MIT, showing improved seizure detection accuracy and interpretability.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the external knowledge base and retrieval step, which may limit generalization if clinical knowledge is incomplete or biased.
paper_title: NeuroGRIP: Retrieval-Augmented Graph Refinement for Knowledge-Grounded EEG Seizure Diagnosis
